ChatGPT said:

Got it — you want a geography quiz game that:

  1. Starts with the player choosing a continent (e.g., Africa).

  2. Displays a map of that continent, with country borders but no names.

  3. When the player presses Start, a highlight color (like orange) moves randomly across countries, stops at one, and asks the player to type the country’s name.

  4. If the player is correct → the country turns green, plays a “ding”/bell sound, and shows a tick.

  5. If the player is wrong → it turns red, plays a “buzzer” sound, and shows a cross.

  6. Countries are chosen randomly without repetition until all are covered.

  7. It can later extend to other continents.

To achieve this, the best approach is to use:

  • HTML + CSS + JavaScript

  • SVG map of Africa (or other continents) — each country as an <path> element with a unique id.

  • JavaScript to control the random selection, color transitions, input checking, and sounds.

Here’s a working starter code for the Africa map quiz, which you can expand later for other continents.

🌍 index.html

html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Geography Quiz Game</title>
  <style>
    body {
      font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
      text-align: center;
      background-color: #f4f4f4;
    }
    svg {
      width: 70%;
      height: auto;
      border: 2px solid #333;
      margin-top: 20px;
    }
    #controls {
      margin: 15px 0;
    }
    #status {
      font-size: 18px;
      font-weight: bold;
    }
    .correct {
      color: green;
    }
    .wrong {
      color: red;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Geography Quiz: Africa</h1>
  <div id="controls">
    <button id="startBtn">Start</button>
    <input type="text" id="answer" placeholder="Enter country name" />
    <button id="submitBtn">Submit</button>
    <p id="status"></p>
  </div>

  <!-- Simplified SVG Map of Africa -->
  <!-- For full accuracy, replace this with a detailed SVG map of Africa -->
  <svg id="africaMap" viewBox="0 0 800 800">
    <path id="ug" d="M400 500 L420 520 L410 540 L390 540 Z" fill="#ccc" stroke="#333" />
    <path id="ke" d="M420 520 L440 520 L440 540 L410 540 Z" fill="#ccc" stroke="#333" />
    <path id="tz" d="M410 540 L440 540 L440 560 L410 560 Z" fill="#ccc" stroke="#333" />
    <path id="sd" d="M400 460 L440 460 L440 480 L400 480 Z" fill="#ccc" stroke="#333" />
  </svg>

  <audio id="correctSound" src="https://actions.google.com/sounds/v1/alarms/digital_watch_alarm_long.ogg"></audio>
  <audio id="wrongSound" src="https://actions.google.com/sounds/v1/cartoon/clang_and_wobble.ogg"></audio>

  <script>
    const countries = {
      ug: "uganda",
      ke: "kenya",
      tz: "tanzania",
      sd: "sudan"
    };

    const paths = Object.keys(countries);
    let current = null;
    const africaMap = document.getElementById("africaMap");
    const status = document.getElementById("status");
    const answer = document.getElementById("answer");
    const correctSound = document.getElementById("correctSound");
    const wrongSound = document.getElementById("wrongSound");

    function pickRandomCountry() {
      if (paths.length === 0) {
        status.textContent = "🎉 All countries done!";
        return null;
      }
      const index = Math.floor(Math.random() * paths.length);
      return paths[index];
    }

    function highlightCountry(id, color) {
      africaMap.querySelectorAll("path").forEach(p => p.setAttribute("fill", "#ccc"));
      document.getElementById(id).setAttribute("fill", color);
    }

    document.getElementById("startBtn").addEventListener("click", () => {
      current = pickRandomCountry();
      if (current) {
        highlightCountry(current, "orange");
        status.textContent = "Guess the country!";
        answer.value = "";
        answer.focus();
      }
    });

    document.getElementById("submitBtn").addEventListener("click", () => {
      if (!current) return;
      const userAns = answer.value.trim().toLowerCase();
      if (userAns === countries[current]) {
        highlightCountry(current, "green");
        status.textContent = "✅ Correct!";
        status.className = "correct";
        correctSound.play();
      } else {
        highlightCountry(current, "red");
        status.textContent = `❌ Wrong! It was ${countries[current].toUpperCase()}`;
        status.className = "wrong";
        wrongSound.play();
      }
      paths.splice(paths.indexOf(current), 1);
      current = null;
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>

🔧 How it works:

  • You’ll need to replace the SVG paths with a full Africa SVG map (each country as a <path>).

  • Each path must have an ID (e.g., ug for Uganda, ke for Kenya).

  • The script picks a random country, highlights it orange, asks the question, and gives feedback with sound and color.

Nice — I built a complete, single-file geography quiz that:

  • Lets the student pick a continent (starts with Africa).

  • Loads a real SVG map of the continent (country borders visible, not labelled).

  • Randomly “moves” a highlight (orange) across country shapes and stops on a country.

  • Prompts the student to type the country’s name; correct → green + bell + tick; wrong → red + buzzer + cross.

  • Picks countries at random without repetition until the pool is exhausted.

  • Extracts country names from the SVG itself (so you don’t have to hand-fill path lists).

  • Is extendable to other continents by adding SVG URLs.

Important note on the SVG used: I load a freely-licensed SVG of Africa from Wikimedia Commons (used under CC BY-SA). If your browser blocks cross-origin SVG fetches from Wikimedia, the page will tell you and give a fallback instruction to download the SVG and put it next to the HTML file. (If you want, I can paste an inline SVG instead — it’s big and would make the HTML very long. This approach keeps the file tidy and uses the official blank Africa map.) <!doctype html>

<head>

  body{margin:0;font-family:Inter,system-ui,Arial,sans-serif;background:var(--bg);color:#111}

<body>
<header>
  <div class="wrap">
    <h1>Continent Map Quiz</h1>
    <p class="lead">Choose a continent, press Start — watch the highlight move, then type the country name.</p>

</header>

<main class="wrap">
  <div class="controls">
    <label>
      Continent:
      <select id="continentSelect">
        <option value="africa" selected>Africa</option>
        <!-- placeholders for extendability -->

        <option value="europe">Europe (add SVG)</option>
        <option value="americas">Americas (add SVG)</option>
        <option value="oceania">Oceania (add SVG)</option>
      </select>
    </label>

    <button id="loadMapBtn">Load Map</button>
    <button id="startBtn" disabled>Start Round</button>

    <div id="gameState" style="margin-left:auto; font-size:13px;color:var(--muted)">

    </div>

        Map will appear here after loading.<br/><small>Click "Load Map" to fetch the continent SVG.</small>
      </div>
    </div>

    <aside id="panel">
      <div class="big">Quiz Panel</div>
      <div class="stat" id="currentCountryLabel">Current target: <strong id="targetName">—</strong></div>
      <div id="promptArea">

          <input id="answerInput" type="text" placeholder="Country name" autocomplete="off" />
          <button id="submitBtn" disabled>Submit</button>
        </div>
        <div id="feedback" class="status"></div>
      </div>

      <div class="credits">
        SVG source: Wikimedia Commons (blank Africa map). Use of that SVG requires attribution when redistributed. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
      </div>

      <div style="margin-top:12px">
        <button id="resetBtn">Reset Game</button>
      </div>

    </aside>
  </div>

  <footer>
    Tip: If the map doesn't load due to CORS, download the Africa SVG (File: Africa_countries.svg from Wikimedia Commons) and place it as <code>africa.svg</code> next to this HTML file — the page will fall back to loading it locally.
  </footer>
</main>

<!-- sounds -->
<audio id="sndCorrect" preload="auto" src="https://actions.google.com/sounds/v1/alarms/digital_watch_alarm_long.ogg"></audio>
<audio id="sndWrong" preload="auto" src="https://actions.google.com/sounds/v1/alarms/beep_short.ogg"></audio>

<script>
/*
  How this works (short):
  - Load an SVG for the selected continent (for Africa we point to Wikimedia Commons file).
  - Parse SVG and extract country-shaped elements that have an associated <title> or id.
  - Build a pool of countries. Start -> an animated random walk highlights many countries quickly and then stops on a chosen one.
  - The user types a name. We normalize both strings (remove diacritics, punctuation, whitespace) and compare.
  - Correct -> green, bell sound, tick. Wrong -> red, buzzer, show correct name.
  - Countries are removed from pool after attempted answer (no repetition).
*/

const continentMapUrls = {
  africa: 'https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/Africa_countries.svg',
  // add more urls for other continents (Wikimedia or other hosts that permit CORS)
};

const container = document.getElementById('svgContainer');
const loadMapBtn = document.getElementById('loadMapBtn');
const continentSelect = document.getElementById('continentSelect');
const startBtn = document.getElementById('startBtn');
const submitBtn = document.getElementById('submitBtn');
const answerInput = document.getElementById('answerInput');
const targetNameLabel = document.getElementById('targetName');
const feedback = document.getElementById('feedback');
const remainingLabel = document.getElementById('remaining');
const resetBtn = document.getElementById('resetBtn');

const sndCorrect = document.getElementById('sndCorrect');
const sndWrong = document.getElementById('sndWrong');

let countryElements = []; // {el, name, id}
let remaining = [];
let currentTarget = null;
let svgRoot = null;

// helper: normalize strings for forgiving comparison
function normalizeName(s){
  if(!s) return '';
  s = s.toLowerCase().trim();
  // remove diacritics
  s = s.normalize('NFD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '');
  // remove punctuation
  s = s.replace(/['"‘’“”–—(),.\/:;]/g,'');
  // common replacements
  s = s.replace(/\bthe\b/g,'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim();
  return s;
}

// Extract country shapes from loaded SVG: look for <path>, <polygon>, <g> that contain <title> or id
function extractCountriesFromSVG(svgDoc){
  const shapes = [];
  // Common patterns: path, polygon, g elements that represent country shapes
  const possible = svgDoc.querySelectorAll('path, polygon, g');
  possible.forEach(node=>{
    // skip strokes/land-sea elements which might not have geographic id/title
    const titleElem = node.querySelector && node.querySelector('title');
    let name = titleElem ? titleElem.textContent : null;
    // fallback: id attribute often contains ISO or country name
    const id = node.getAttribute ? node.getAttribute('id') : null;
    if(!name && id){
      // sometimes the title is missing; use id but not things like 'ocean' or 'background'
      name = id;
    }
    if(name){
      // basic filter: ignore obvious non-country ids
      const skip = ['ocean','background','land','water','frame','continent'];
      const lname = (name||'').toLowerCase();
      if(skip.some(s=>lname.includes(s))) return;
      shapes.push({el: node, name: name.trim(), id: id || null});
    }
  });

  // remove duplicates (same name multiple times)
  const uniq = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  shapes.forEach(s=>{
    const key = normalizeName(s.name);
    if(!seen.has(key)){
      seen.add(key);
      uniq.push(s);
    }
  });
  return uniq;
}

async function loadSVGForContinent(continent){
  const url = continentMapUrls[continent];
  if(!url) throw new Error('No map URL configured for that continent yet.');
  // try to fetch from remote
  try{
    const resp = await fetch(url);
    if(!resp.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch remote SVG: ' + resp.status);
    const text = await resp.text();
    // parse
    const parser = new DOMParser();
    const doc = parser.parseFromString(text, 'image/svg+xml');
    const svg = doc.documentElement;
    // clean container and inject
    container.innerHTML = '';
    // scale nicely
    svg.setAttribute('width','100%');
    svg.setAttribute('height','auto');
    svg.style.maxWidth = '100%';
    svg.style.display = 'block';
    // Make sure country shapes are pointer-events enabled (for highlight)
    const allPaths = svg.querySelectorAll('path, polygon');
    allPaths.forEach(p=>{
      p.style.fill = '#e6e6e6';
      p.style.stroke = '#999';
      p.style.strokeWidth = '0.6';
      p.style.cursor = 'default';
    });
    // append
    container.appendChild(svg);
    svgRoot = svg;
    return svg;
  }catch(err){
    // fallback: try local file named 'africa.svg'
    console.warn('remote fetch failed',err);
    container.innerHTML = `<div style="padding:24px;color:#800">Could not fetch remote SVG: ${err.message}.<br/>
      Trying fallback: load local <code>${continent}.svg</code> (place it next to this HTML and reload).</div>`;
    throw err;
  }
}

function prepareGameFromSVG(svg){
  // find country shapes
  countryElements = extractCountriesFromSVG(svg);
  // If countryElements seems empty, try other heuristics (some SVGs put titles directly under svg)
  if(countryElements.length === 0){
    // try titles that are direct children of svg and referencing another element via aria-labelledby
    const titles = svg.querySelectorAll('title');
    titles.forEach(t=>{
      const parent = t.parentElement;
      if(parent && (parent.tagName.toLowerCase()==='path' || parent.tagName.toLowerCase()==='g')){
        countryElements.push({el: parent, name: t.textContent, id: parent.getAttribute('id')});
      }
    });
  }

  // normalize and filter further
  countryElements = countryElements.filter(c=>{
    // require a textual name
    return c.name && c.name.trim().length>1;
  });

  // sometimes the SVG groups countries inside <g id="countries"> and has subpaths for little islands; we still include them
  // set default fill
  countryElements.forEach(c=>{
    try{ c.el.style.fill = '#e6e6e6'; c.el.style.opacity = '1'; }catch(e){}
  });

  // build the remaining pool
  remaining = countryElements.slice();

  // update UI
  remainingLabel.textContent = `Countries remaining: ${remaining.length}`;
  startBtn.disabled = remaining.length === 0;
  submitBtn.disabled = true;
  answerInput.value = '';
  targetNameLabel.textContent = '—';
  feedback.textContent = '';
}

// generate a random item from an array (non-destructive)
function sample(arr){ return arr[Math.floor(Math.random()*arr.length)]; }

// animate the moving highlight: picks a sequence of elements and highlights them quickly before stopping on target
async function animateRandomWalk(targetEl){
  // generate a shuffled sequence of elements (fast moves), ending with the target
  const steps = [];
  const pool = countryElements.slice();
  // create N steps (more steps => longer animation). We'll pick random elements, allow repeats for "moving" feel.
  const N = Math.min(28, Math.max(12, Math.floor(12 + Math.random()*16)));
  for(let i=0;i<N;i++){
    steps.push(sample(pool));
  }
  // ensure last is target
  steps.push({el: targetEl});
  // timing pattern: accelerate then sudden stop
  let t = 40;
  for(let i=0;i<steps.length;i++){
    const step = steps[i];
    highlightMoving(step.el);
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, t));
    // slightly increase delay towards end to simulate stopping
    t += Math.floor((i/steps.length) * 60);
  }
}

// highlight for moving (orange)
function highlightMoving(el){
  // clear previous moving highlights
  if(!svgRoot) return;
  svgRoot.querySelectorAll('path, polygon, g').forEach(node=>{
    // only reduce color for nodes in our countryElements list; otherwise leave alone
    node.style.opacity = '1';
    // set back to default if not flagged as answered
    if(!node.dataset.answered){
      node.style.fill = '#e6e6e6';
    }
  });
  try{
    // Some shapes are grouped (<g>); if el is a <g> highlight its children
    if(el.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'g'){
      const children = el.querySelectorAll('path, polygon, rect');
      children.forEach(c=> c.style.fill = 'var(--accent)');
      el.style.fill = 'var(--accent)';
    } else {
      el.style.fill = 'var(--accent)';
    }
  }catch(e){}
}

// mark final result: correct or wrong
function markResult(el, correct){
  // mark answered to avoid re-highlighting
  function colorNode(node, color){
    try{ node.style.fill = color; node.dataset.answered = '1'; }catch(e){}
  }
  if(el.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'g'){
    const children = el.querySelectorAll('path, polygon, rect');
    children.forEach(c=> colorNode(c, correct ? 'var(--correct)' : 'var(--wrong)'));
    colorNode(el, correct ? 'var(--correct)' : 'var(--wrong)');
  } else {
    colorNode(el, correct ? 'var(--correct)' : 'var(--wrong)');
  }
}

// pick a random target from remaining pool (no repetition)
function pickTarget(){
  if(remaining.length === 0) return null;
  const idx = Math.floor(Math.random()*remaining.length);
  return remaining[idx];
}

loadMapBtn.addEventListener('click', async ()=>{
  const cont = continentSelect.value;
  loadMapBtn.disabled = true;
  loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Loading...';
  try{
    const svg = await loadSVGForContinent(cont);
    // small tweak: remove any inline <style> that hides titles (we want titles readable programmatically)
    // next prepare the game
    prepareGameFromSVG(svg);
    // try to show which country elements were recognized (optional)
    loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Loaded ✓';
    setTimeout(()=> loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Reload Map', 1200);
  }catch(err){
    // fetch failed (handled in loadSVGForContinent)
    loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Load Map';
    console.error(err);
    alert('Could not load remote SVG. See console. If CORS prevents loading, download the SVG (File: Africa_countries.svg from Wikimedia Commons) and save it as "africa.svg" next to this HTML file, then reload.');
  } finally{
    loadMapBtn.disabled = false;
  }
});

startBtn.addEventListener('click', async ()=>{
  feedback.textContent = '';
  // pick a target from remaining
  const chosen = pickTarget();
  if(!chosen){
    feedback.textContent = 'No countries remaining — reset to play again.';
    return;
  }
  currentTarget = chosen;
  // animate movement (fast highlight)
  startBtn.disabled = true;
  answerInput.disabled = true;
  submitBtn.disabled = true;
  await animateRandomWalk(chosen.el);
  // reveal prompt
  targetNameLabel.textContent = '—'; // we don't show the answer
  answerInput.value = '';
  answerInput.disabled = false;
  answerInput.focus();
  submitBtn.disabled = false;
});

submitBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(!currentTarget) return;
  const user = normalizeName(answerInput.value || '');
  const actual = normalizeName(currentTarget.name || '');
  // small alias mapping (common names). Add more aliases here as needed.
  const aliases = {
    'cote divoire': 'ivory coast',
    'cotedivoire': 'ivory coast',
    'ivory coast': 'ivory coast',
    'eswatini': 'swaziland',
    'swaziland': 'swaziland',
    'congo republic': 'congo',
    'congo drc': 'democratic republic of the congo',
    'drc': 'democratic republic of the congo',
    "democratic republic of the congo": "democratic republic of the congo",
    "republic of congo": "congo"
  };
  const resolvedUser = aliases[user] || user;
  const resolvedActual = aliases[actual] || actual;

  let ok = false;
  // exact match
  if(resolvedUser === resolvedActual) ok = true;
  // also allow answers that are a substring if names are long (user typed 'niger' and actual is 'niger' -> ok already)
  // otherwise check partial
  if(!ok && resolvedUser && resolvedActual && (resolvedUser.includes(resolvedActual) || resolvedActual.includes(resolvedUser))) {
    ok = true;
  }

  if(ok){
    // correct
    markResult(currentTarget.el, true);
    sndCorrect.currentTime = 0; sndCorrect.play().catch(()=>{});
    feedback.innerHTML = `<span style="color:var(--correct)">✅ Correct</span> <span class="resultIcon">✔️</span>`;
  }else{
    markResult(currentTarget.el, false);
    sndWrong.currentTime = 0; sndWrong.play().catch(()=>{});
    feedback.innerHTML = `<span style="color:var(--wrong)">❌ Wrong — it was <strong>${currentTarget.name}</strong></span> <span class="resultIcon">✖️</span>`;
  }

  // remove this one from remaining (so no repetition)
  remaining = remaining.filter(r => r !== currentTarget);
  remainingLabel.textContent = `Countries remaining: ${remaining.length}`;
  currentTarget = null;
  answerInput.value = '';
  submitBtn.disabled = true;
  answerInput.disabled = true;
  startBtn.disabled = remaining.length === 0;
  if(remaining.length === 0){
    feedback.innerHTML += '<div style="margin-top:8px">🎉 You have attempted all recognized countries.</div>';
  }
});

answerInput.addEventListener('keydown', (e)=>{
  if(e.key === 'Enter' && !submitBtn.disabled){
    submitBtn.click();
  }
});

resetBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(!svgRoot) return;
  // reset styles
  svgRoot.querySelectorAll('path, polygon, g').forEach(node=>{
    node.style.fill = '#e6e6e6';
    node.dataset.answered = '';
  });
  prepareGameFromSVG(svgRoot);
});

// small helper: if the user changes continent, disable start until reloaded
continentSelect.addEventListener('change', ()=>{
  startBtn.disabled = true;
  // you can optionally auto-load the new continent's map
});

// When the SVG is present and user presses reload, enable start button
// Also try auto-load Africa on first page open
(async function init(){
  // auto-load Africa map
  try {
    loadMapBtn.click();
    // after a second, enable start if countries parsed
    setTimeout(()=>{
      if(remaining.length>0) startBtn.disabled = false;
    }, 1400);
  }catch(e){}
})();

</script>
</body>
</html>

1) What the CORS tip means (simple)

  • When your browser loads a page from yourdomain.com and tries to fetch an SVG hosted on upload.wikimedia.org, the browser checks CORS headers on the remote server. If those headers don’t explicitly allow your page origin, the fetch is blocked → no map.

  • Fixes:

    • Best: host the SVG on the same origin as your page (e.g., yourdomain.com/maps/africa.svg) → no CORS issues.

    • Alternate: have your server fetch (proxy) the Wikimedia SVG and re-serve it (the browser then fetches from your origin).

    • Fallback: download the SVG and place it beside index.html and fetch locally (works offline or during dev).

2) Where to get the Africa SVG

  • Wikimedia Commons has Africa_countries.svg (free, but check license if you redistribute). Download the file and name it africa.svg (or maps/africa.svg) and place it in your site’s public folder.

3) server.js — Express server that serves static files and optionally proxies the Wikimedia SVG

Save as server.js. Assumes Node 18+ (has fetch builtin). If older Node, install node-fetch.

js
// server.js
import express from "express";
import path from "path";
import fs from "fs";

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3000;

// Serve your static front-end files from "public/"
app.use(express.static(path.join(process.cwd(), "public")));

// Option A: If you downloaded africa.svg and put in public/maps/africa.svg,
// the browser can fetch "/maps/africa.svg" with no CORS issues.
//
// Option B (proxy): If you want the server to fetch the Wikimedia SVG and serve it
// so the client never contacts Wikimedia (also avoids CORS on client side):
app.get("/maps/africa-proxy.svg", async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const remoteUrl = "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/Africa_countries.svg";
    // server-side fetch
    const response = await fetch(remoteUrl);
    if (!response.ok) {
      res.status(502).send("Failed to fetch remote SVG");
      return;
    }
    const svgText = await response.text();
    // Optional: cache locally to disk to avoid repeated fetches
    // fs.writeFileSync(path.join(process.cwd(), 'public','maps','africa.svg'), svgText, 'utf8');

    res.setHeader("Content-Type", "image/svg+xml");
    // optionally set caching headers
    res.setHeader("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=86400");
    res.send(svgText);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("proxy error:", err);
    res.status(500).send("Server error");
  }
});

app.listen(PORT, () => console.log(`Server running on http://localhost:${PORT}`));

    /maps

# Node 18+ has fetch; if Node < 18 you must install node-fetch and adjust server.js

# open http://localhost:3000

Use /maps/africa.svg (local static) in your index.html, or /maps/africa-proxy.svg if you prefer proxying.

This is the frontend file — it uses the same UI/design you liked and injects the real map into the container. It first tries the Wikimedia URL (fast if CORS allows it), then falls back to /maps/africa.svg (local file you downloaded), and finally shows instructions if both fail.

Save as public/index.html.

html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8"/>
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"/>
<title>Continent Map Quiz — Africa (with real SVG)</title>
<style>
  :root{
    --bg:#f6f7fb; --accent:#ff8c2e; --muted:#666; --panel:#fff;
    --correct:#28a745; --wrong:#dc3545; --map-border:#222;
  }
  body{margin:0;font-family:Arial,Segoe UI,system-ui;background:var(--bg);color:#111}
  .wrap{max-width:1100px;margin:18px auto;padding:18px}
  header{padding:18px}
  h1{margin:0;font-size:20px}
  .controls{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;margin:12px 0;flex-wrap:wrap}
  select,input,button{padding:8px;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #d6d9e6;background:white}
  #mapWrap{display:flex;gap:18px;align-items:flex-start}
  #svgContainer{flex:1;border:2px solid var(--map-border);background:#fff;padding:8px;border-radius:8px;min-height:480px;overflow:auto}
  #panel{width:320px;padding:12px;border-radius:8px;background:var(--panel);box-shadow:0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.06)}
  .stat{font-size:13px;color:var(--muted)}
  .big{font-weight:700;margin-bottom:8px}
  .status{font-weight:700;margin-top:10px}
</style>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="wrap">
    <header>
      <h1>Continent Map Quiz</h1>
      <p class="stat">Click <strong>Load Map</strong>, then <strong>Start Round</strong>. The highlight will move and stop on a country.</p>
    </header>

    <div class="controls">
      <select id="continentSelect"><option value="africa">Africa</option></select>
      <button id="loadMapBtn">Load Map</button>
      <button id="startBtn" disabled>Start Round</button>
      <div style="margin-left:auto" class="stat" id="remaining">Countries remaining: —</div>
    </div>

    <div id="mapWrap">
      <div id="svgContainer" aria-live="polite">
        <div id="placeholder" style="padding:40px;text-align:center;color:var(--muted)">
          Map will appear here after loading.<br/><small>Click "Load Map" to fetch the continent SVG.</small>
        </div>
      </div>

      <aside id="panel">
        <div class="big">Quiz Panel</div>
        <div class="stat">Type the country's name:</div>
        <input id="answerInput" type="text" placeholder="country name" style="width:100%;margin-top:8px" disabled/>
        <div style="margin-top:8px">
          <button id="submitBtn" disabled>Submit</button>
          <button id="resetBtn">Reset</button>
        </div>
        <div id="feedback" class="status"></div>
      </aside>
    </div>

    <footer style="margin-top:12px;font-size:12px;color:var(--muted)">
      Tip: If remote fails, place <code>africa.svg</code> in <code>/public/maps/</code> and reload.
    </footer>
  </div>

  <audio id="sndCorrect" src="https://actions.google.com/sounds/v1/alarms/digital_watch_alarm_long.ogg"></audio>
  <audio id="sndWrong" src="https://actions.google.com/sounds/v1/alarms/beep_short.ogg"></audio>

<script>
const wikimediaUrl = "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/92/Africa_countries.svg";
// local path (put the downloaded file here)
const localPath = "/maps/africa.svg";
// or use the server proxy: /maps/africa-proxy.svg (if you used server.js proxy)
const proxyPath = "/maps/africa-proxy.svg";

const loadMapBtn = document.getElementById('loadMapBtn');
const svgContainer = document.getElementById('svgContainer');
const placeholder = document.getElementById('placeholder');
const startBtn = document.getElementById('startBtn');
const remainingLabel = document.getElementById('remaining');
const submitBtn = document.getElementById('submitBtn');
const answerInput = document.getElementById('answerInput');
const resetBtn = document.getElementById('resetBtn');
const feedback = document.getElementById('feedback');
const sndCorrect = document.getElementById('sndCorrect');
const sndWrong = document.getElementById('sndWrong');

let svgRoot = null;
let countryElements = []; // {el, name}
let remaining = [];
let current = null;

function normalize(s){ return s ? s.toLowerCase().normalize('NFD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g,'').replace(/[^a-z0-9 ]/g,'').trim() : ''; }

async function fetchSvgText(url){
  const res = await fetch(url, {cache: "no-store"}); // cache disabled for dev
  if(!res.ok) throw new Error('fetch failed: ' + res.status);
  return await res.text();
}

// Try remote then proxy then local
async function loadMap(){
  loadMapBtn.disabled = true;
  loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Loading...';
  svgContainer.innerHTML = '<div style="padding:40px;text-align:center;color:#666">Loading map…</div>';

  const sources = [wikimediaUrl, proxyPath, localPath];
  let lastErr = null;
  for(const src of sources){
    try{
      const text = await fetchSvgText(src);
      // parse the SVG
      const parser = new DOMParser();
      const doc = parser.parseFromString(text, "image/svg+xml");
      const svg = doc.documentElement;
      // ensure width responsive
      svg.setAttribute('width','100%');
      svg.setAttribute('height','auto');
      svg.style.display = 'block';
      // reset container and inject
      svgContainer.innerHTML = '';
      svgContainer.appendChild(svg);
      svgRoot = svg;
      prepareFromSvg(svg);
      loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Loaded ✓';
      startBtn.disabled = remaining.length === 0;
      setTimeout(()=> loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Reload Map', 1200);
      return;
    }catch(err){
      lastErr = err;
      console.warn('failed to load', src, err);
    }
  }

  // all failed
  svgContainer.innerHTML = `<div style="padding:24px;color:#800">Could not load the map from remote or local sources. Console shows details. If you downloaded the SVG to <code>/public/maps/africa.svg</code>, make sure your server serves it. Error: ${lastErr?.message||'unknown'}</div>`;
  loadMapBtn.disabled = false;
  loadMapBtn.textContent = 'Load Map';
}

// extract country shapes (heuristic)
function extractCountries(svg){
  const items = [];
  const nodes = svg.querySelectorAll('path, polygon, g');
  nodes.forEach(n=>{
    // try title
    let title = '';
    const t = n.querySelector && n.querySelector('title');
    if(t) title = t.textContent;
    if(!title){
      // fallback to id or aria-label
      title = n.getAttribute('id') || n.getAttribute('aria-label') || n.getAttribute('inkscape:label') || '';
    }
    if(title && title.length>1){
      items.push({el: n, name: title});
    }
  });

  // unique by normalized name
  const map = new Map();
  items.forEach(it=>{
    const key = normalize(it.name);
    if(!map.has(key)) map.set(key, it);
  });
  return Array.from(map.values());
}

function prepareFromSvg(svg){
  // basic styling defaults
  svg.querySelectorAll('path,polygon').forEach(p=>{
    p.style.fill = '#e6e6e6';
    p.style.stroke = '#999';
    p.style.strokeWidth = '0.5';
  });
  countryElements = extractCountries(svg);
  remaining = countryElements.slice();
  remainingLabel.textContent = `Countries remaining: ${remaining.length}`;
  feedback.textContent = '';
  answerInput.disabled = true;
  submitBtn.disabled = true;
  startBtn.disabled = remaining.length === 0;
}

// animate a quick random movement then stop at target
async function animateToTarget(targetEl){
  const steps = [];
  const total = Math.min(28, Math.max(12, 12 + Math.floor(Math.random()*18)));
  for(let i=0;i<total;i++){
    steps.push(remaining[Math.floor(Math.random()*remaining.length)]);
  }
  steps.push({el: targetEl}); // final stop
  let delay = 40;
  for(let i=0;i<steps.length;i++){
    highlightMoving(steps[i].el);
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, delay));
    delay += Math.floor((i/steps.length)*60);
  }
}

function highlightMoving(el){
  // reset non-answered fills
  svgRoot.querySelectorAll('path,polygon,g').forEach(n=>{
    if(!n.dataset.answered) n.style.fill = '#e6e6e6';
  });
  if(el.tagName.toLowerCase()==='g'){
    el.querySelectorAll('path,polygon').forEach(c=> c.style.fill = 'var(--accent)');
    el.style.fill = 'var(--accent)';
  } else {
    el.style.fill = 'var(--accent)';
  }
}

function markResult(el, ok){
  if(el.tagName.toLowerCase()==='g'){
    el.querySelectorAll('path,polygon').forEach(c=> { c.style.fill = ok ? 'var(--correct)' : 'var(--wrong)'; c.dataset.answered='1'; });
  } else {
    el.style.fill = ok ? 'var(--correct)' : 'var(--wrong)';
    el.dataset.answered = '1';
  }
}

function pickTarget(){
  if(remaining.length===0) return null;
  const idx = Math.floor(Math.random()*remaining.length);
  return remaining[idx];
}

loadMapBtn.addEventListener('click', loadMap);

startBtn.addEventListener('click', async ()=>{
  current = pickTarget();
  if(!current) {
    feedback.textContent = 'No countries left';
    return;
  }
  // animate
  startBtn.disabled = true;
  answerInput.disabled = true;
  submitBtn.disabled = true;
  await animateToTarget(current.el);
  // prompt player
  answerInput.disabled = false;
  submitBtn.disabled = false;
  answerInput.focus();
});

submitBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(!current) return;
  const user = normalize(answerInput.value);
  const actual = normalize(current.name);
  const ok = (user === actual) || (user && actual.includes(user)) || (user && user.includes(actual));
  if(ok){
    markResult(current.el, true);
    sndCorrect.currentTime = 0; sndCorrect.play().catch(()=>{});
    feedback.innerHTML = `<span style="color:var(--correct)">✅ Correct</span>`;
  } else {
    markResult(current.el, false);
    sndWrong.currentTime = 0; sndWrong.play().catch(()=>{});
    feedback.innerHTML = `<span style="color:var(--wrong)">❌ Wrong — it was <strong>${current.name}</strong></span>`;
  }
  // remove from remaining
  remaining = remaining.filter(r=> r !== current);
  remainingLabel.textContent = `Countries remaining: ${remaining.length}`;
  current = null;
  answerInput.value = '';
  submitBtn.disabled = true;
  answerInput.disabled = true;
  startBtn.disabled = remaining.length === 0;
});

resetBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(!svgRoot) return;
  svgRoot.querySelectorAll('path,polygon,g').forEach(n=>{
    n.style.fill = '#e6e6e6';
    n.dataset.answered = '';
  });
  countryElements = extractCountries(svgRoot);
  remaining = countryElements.slice();
  remainingLabel.textContent = `Countries remaining: ${remaining.length}`;
  feedback.textContent = '';
  startBtn.disabled = remaining.length === 0;
});

// optional: allow Enter to submit
answerInput.addEventListener('keydown', (e)=> {
  if(e.key === 'Enter' && !submitBtn.disabled) submitBtn.click();
});
</script>
</body>
</html>

Summary — what the game is

A student picks a continent → the page displays the continent map with country borders (no labels) → the student presses Start → a highlighted color (orange-ish) moves randomly across country shapes and stops on one → the game prompts the student to type the country name → correct answer = the country turns green, a pleasant bell plays and a tick appears; wrong answer = country turns red, a buzzer plays and the correct name is shown. Countries are chosen randomly without repetition until the pool is exhausted. The design is school-friendly, responsive, and can be extended to other continents or logged to a backend.

Main pieces you need

  1. HTML/CSS/JS frontend — UI, map container, buttons, input, feedback, sounds.

  2. SVG map files — one SVG per continent where each country is a shape (<path>, <g>, <polygon>) with a readable name (usually in a <title> or id).

  3. Map loading logic — try remote SVG → fallback to local file → fallback to inline SVG.

  4. Country extraction code — parse the SVG, build a [{el, name}] list programmatically.

  5. Game logic — pick random country from remaining set, animate highlight moving between shapes, prompt, check answer (normalize names), mark result, remove from pool.

  6. Optional server — to serve static files or proxy the remote SVG and avoid CORS issues (Express example provided earlier).

  7. Assets — short sound files for correct/wrong and optionally icons for tick/cross.

Step-by-step “how to do it” (developer checklist)

  1. Prepare project structure

    • your-project/

      • public/index.html ← frontend HTML + JS (single-file app)

      • public/maps/africa.svg ← downloaded SVG (recommended)

      • server.js ← optional Express server to host files / proxy SVGs

  2. Get the SVG(s)

    • Download Africa_countries.svg (or other continent SVGs) from Wikimedia Commons and save as public/maps/africa.svg.

    • Option: embed SVG inline into index.html to guarantee it always appears (makes HTML large).

  3. Frontend behavior

    • On Load Map: fetch wikimedia → if blocked by CORS, fetch /maps/africa.svg (local) or /maps/africa-proxy.svg (server proxy).

    • Parse the SVG DOM and find country shapes (check <title>, id, aria-label).

    • Build remaining = [countries].

    • On Start Round:

      • pick target = random(remaining)

      • animate: highlight many countries quickly (random), then stop on target

      • enable text input and Submit

    • On Submit:

      • normalize both user input and target name (lowercase, remove diacritics/punctuation)

      • match exact, allow common aliases and partial matches

      • correct → fill shape green, play bell, show tick

      • wrong → fill shape red, play buzzer, show cross + reveal correct name

      • remove target from remaining

    • Repeat until remaining is empty

  4. Server (optional but recommended for production/dev)

    • Static serve public/ so fetch('/maps/africa.svg') is same-origin (no CORS).

    • Or provide /maps/africa-proxy.svg that fetches Wikimedia server-side and returns the SVG (also avoids CORS in client).

    • Basic Express server provided earlier — run node server.js.

  5. Polish

    • Add synonyms/aliases mapping (Côte d’Ivoire → Ivory Coast; Eswatini → Swaziland, etc.).

    • Add scoring, timer, hint system, and teacher export (CSV).

    • Accessibility: make keyboard submit (Enter), provide alt text, ARIA live regions for feedback.

    • Mobile: ensure SVG scales, large tappable buttons.

    • Sounds: short, unobtrusive; allow user to mute.

Quick developer commands

  • Install and run server (example):

    bash
    npm init -y
npm i express
node server.js
# open http://localhost:3000

  • If testing without a server, use a static dev server:

    bash
    npx serve public
# or: npx http-server public

Common pitfalls & how to fix them

  • Map doesn’t load (CORS): browser blocked fetch to Wikimedia. Fixes:

    • Serve the SVG from your own server (/maps/africa.svg) — recommended.

    • what is better for an ai to view codes? .pdf, .docx, .odt, .rtf, .txt, .html(zipped), .epub, .md which way is better
  • Copy
    • AITOPIA
    When considering the best format for an AI to view and analyze code, here are some considerations for the given formats:
    1. Plain Text Formats:
      • .txt: This is the simplest format, containing raw text without any formatting. It is easy for AI to read and parse.
      • .md (Markdown): Similar to .txt, but allows for simple formatting (like headings, lists). The syntax is straightforward, making it easy for AI to process while still being human-readable.
    2. Code-Specific Formats:
      • .html: If the code is already in HTML, it can be easy for an AI to process it as web browsers can render it directly. Zipping it (e.g., .html zipped) may add complexity and is generally not necessary unless you're trying to save space or bundle multiple files.
    3. Document Formats:
      • .pdf: Good for sharing, but parsing PDFs can be challenging for AI due to potential formatting issues and not being structured text.
      • .docx and .odt: These formats are more complex because they contain additional metadata and formatting, which can complicate parsing for AI.

  • Copy
    • AITOPIA
    It looks like you're trying to create a link that redirects users to the "teacherdashboard.html" page. Here's a cleaner and more user-friendly way to write it using proper HTML syntax:
    <a href="teacherdashboard.html">Go to Teacher Dashboard</a>
    If you want to use JavaScript to navigate to the new page programmatically (like your original intention), you can use the following approach: 
    <a href="#" onclick="window.location.href='teacherdashboard.html'; return false;">Go to Teacher Dashboard</a>

    Explanation:

    • Using the <a> tag with href: This is the standard way to create a hyperlink that takes users to another page.
    • JavaScript with onclick: This method provides flexibility for additional functionality (like running other scripts) but requires careful handling to prevent the default link behavior (hence the return false;).
    Choose the method based on your requirements!
